newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-DEL PIERO ADVERT PROMPTS BAD TASTE CHARGES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEL PIERO ADVERT PROMPTS BAD TASTE CHARGES.

text.p: A newspaper advertisement placed by the sponsors of Italy striker Alessandro Del Piero caused controversy on Thursday amid accusations of poor taste.
The Adidas advert showed the Juventus player above the words "Only one man can stop him from scoring. Cesare Maldini."
Maldini is the national team coach.
Del Piero, top scorer at the Tournoi de France tournament which ended on Wednesday, had been out of the Italian team since February after suffering a leg muscle injury.

The Corriere dello Sport newspaper called the advertisment a "gaffe", saying that it was unthinkable for a coach to be put under pressure by a player's sponsor. morrow if every sponsor decided to follow the highly-debatable example," it said.
"How many sponsors would buy newspaper pages to suggest their own players to the team coach?"
Maldini was widely quoted as saying that he was amused by the advert and had not known about it in advance.
But Del Piero's agent Claudio Pasqualin told the ANSA news agency that the publicity was in bad taste. "The player and myself are mortified," he said.

"A sponsor should never get involved in the technical side, apart from the dubious taste of the phrase in itself and the fact that we were not even warned about the plan to place such an advertisement in the newspapers."
